chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a pregnant woman whose husband divorces her and then she miscarries, whether the miscarriage was fully formed or not, or she delivered a lump of flesh: does her waiting period end by that? So he said:
Everything that she delivers which makes it clear that it was a pregnancy, whether fully formed or not, then her waiting period has ended by it, even if it was a lump of flesh.

He said: And I heard him saying: If a man divorces his wife and she claims pregnancy, she waits nine months. Then if she gives birth, otherwise she observes a waiting period of three months; then she has become separated from him.

key_terms.تِسْعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ: nine months as the period awaited for a claimed pregnancy
key_terms.مُضْغَةً: a lump of flesh indicating an early-stage fetus

ai.seo_question: Does the ʿiddah of a divorced pregnant woman end after a miscarriage or an unformed fetus?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the ʿiddah of a divorced pregnant woman. If what she delivers is recognizably a pregnancy, her ʿiddah ends with it, whether fully formed or not; and if pregnancy is only claimed, a period of nine months is awaited, after which three months of ʿiddah are observed if no birth occurs.
